metadata.case_name: LAM YIN MAN v. NG HING CHUEN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.education_level: Completed DSE (May 2012); enrolled in Diploma of International Professional Beauty Therapist (one-year full-time) from around September 2012

source: As a result of the accident, the plaintiff suffered injuries to her head, face and right thigh, and lost her right upper incisor.

The attendance notes show that she was “alert” on arrival and she scored 15/15 on the Glasgow Coma Score suggesting that she was then fully conscious. The provisional diagnosis was “Head injury and amnesia”.
She was admitted to the Department of Neurosurgery of the PMH on the same day for further management.

injuries.description: Multiple facial lacerations and resultant facial scarring
source: There was a 0.5cm laceration over her right eyebrow, a 1-cm laceration over her right nasal bridge and a 1-cm laceration above her right upper mouth corner. The lacerations were cleaned and sutured.

There were multiple scars on the plaintiff’s face. But they are all faint and inconspicuous and can be covered up by cosmetic powder except the 1-cm scar which appears at the right corner of her mouth;
Her wounds had healed with no significant complications.
Her right upper incisor was missing and left upper incisor slightly loosened.
A temporary false tooth was put in for her missing incisor.

injuries.description: Right thigh soft tissue injury / pain
source: She also complained of right thigh pain after the injury but an MRI detected no abnormality.
As a result of the accident, the plaintiff still feels intermittent right thigh pain aggravated by weather changes.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at hip or thigh level

source: Bilateral knee abrasions;

injuries.description: Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
source: The diagnosis is adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood;
The illness was caused by the accident;
The prognosis is good and the intensity of the symptoms would be alleviated after further treatment;
The resulting whole person impairment is 10%.

injuries.description: Incidental femoral bone lesion (not related to the injury)
source: There was an incidental finding of femoral bone lesion but it was not related to the injury. She was referred to the orthopaedic surgeon for investigation.

manifestations.description: Lacerations over right eyebrow, right nasal bridge and above right upper mouth corner (sutured)
Low mood, depression, loss of interest or pleasure, poor sleep, anxiety and irritable emotions
Fear (especially of pedestrian crossings), loss of self-confidence and self-esteem

treatments_received.treatment: Cleaning and suturing of facial lacerations
source: There was a 0.5cm laceration over her right eyebrow, a 1-cm laceration over her right nasal bridge and a 1-cm laceration above her right upper mouth corner. The lacerations were cleaned and sutured.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission and management at Department of Neurosurgery, Princess Margaret Hospital
source: She was admitted to the Department of Neurosurgery of the PMH on the same day for further management.
She also complained of right thigh pain after the injury but an MRI detected no abnormality.
A temporary false tooth was put in for her missing incisor.
On 14 June 2013, the plaintiff attended Three Good Tong CMC for Chinese acupuncture. The diagnosis was post-traumatic stress disorder.

She has attended follow-up sessions since then, roughly on a monthly or bi-monthly basis. The diagnosis was adjustment disorder with depressive symptoms. She has been receiving pharmacological treatment.

treatments_future.treatment: Dental implant for upper right incisor
source: It is also reasonable for the plaintiff to have an implant for the upper right incisor which was knocked out during the accident. She has produced a quotation of $45,600. I would have awarded that sum.
treatments_future.vmis_procedure: Any kind of dental surgery due to injury caused by an Accident

treatments_future.treatment: Plastic surgical treatment to improve facial scars
source: It would be reasonable for the plaintiff to receive treatment to improve the facial scars, as recommended jointly by the plastic surgeons. I would have allowed a sum of $58,000, as estimated.
treatments_future.vmis_procedure: Local excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of skin and subcutaneous tissue

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities (PSLA) award as assessed by the court in the event of liability
Pre-trial loss of earnings as a part-time model awarded (from date of accident to date of trial) $86,450
Loss of congenial employment (career as a model) awarded $30,000
Pre-trial expenses (medical, travelling, tonic food) agreed and awarded $5,540
Future plastic surgical treatment to improve facial scars (estimated) $58,000
Future dental treatment - implant for upper right incisor $45,600
